newsitem.title: USA: Dow slides as interest rates spike higher.
newsitem.headline: Dow slides as interest rates spike higher.

text.p: U.S. blue chips skidded to their steepest loss in nearly a month on Wednesday, rocked by a sharp rise in interest rates.

The Dow industrials tumbled 140 points to close unofficially at 7086. The loss was the Dow's biggest since April 11 and undid nearly all the gains it had tallied during back-to-back record-setting sessions on Monday and Tuesday.
Analysts laid blame for the loss directly at the door of a weak bond market, where the benchmark 30-year bond yield jumped back towards seven percent.

With the majority of corporate earnings reported for the quarter, investors had little choice but to focus on the bond market, where a disappointing auction of 10-year U.S. notes helped push long yields up to 6.97 percent from 6.88 percent.
"When there are no earnings to move the market, the stock market and bond market move in tandem," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.

Financial stocks bore the brunt of the selling, resulting in a three percent slide in the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's bank index. J.P. Morgan & Co Inc dropped 3-1/2 to 101-3/8, the largest fall among the 30 Dow industrials.
The Dow's other financial components also slumped. American Express Co slipped 2-3/8 to 66 and Travelers Group Inc fell 2-1/2 to 54-3/8.
With attention again focused on interest rates, analysts said the market's next turn could quickly put the market's recent fierce rebound to the test.

"Certainly if rates keep rising and volatility keeps going along the way it has, that's going to give investors cause to pause and think about what it is they're doing," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
While financials registered the heaviest losses, few groups were left out of the market's widespead sell-off. Tech stocks ended lower, as did small cap stocks.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers by two-to-one on the New York Stock Exchange, where volume totalled about 500 million shares.

One financial stock that bucked the trend was Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc, which jumped 3-7/8 to 38 on heavy volume of more than seven million shares. Traders cited a wave of rumors linking a number of major banks to a possible acquisition of the Wall Street firm.
Lehman declined to comment on the rumors as a matter of policy.
Fluor Corp fell 8-1/4 to 47-3/4 in NYSE activity after warning late Tuesday it expected to report a fiscal second quarter loss of $70 million, or $0.83 per share.
Transitional Hospitals Corp gained 1-1/8 to 15-1/2 after Vencor Inc launched a $16 per share tender offer for all the company's shares.
Vencor's bid topped a competing $14.55 per share offer for Transitional from privately-held Select Medical Corp. Vencor shares fell 3-1/8 to 39-7/8.
The S&P 500 index fell 12.14 points to 815.62.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 5.39 points to 1322.91.
